newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai stocks end down at 1997 low on fund selling.
newsitem.headline: Thai stocks end down at 1997 low on fund selling.

text.p: The Thai stock market fell on Monday to its lowest level this year on thin turnover as investors, mostly local mutual funds, sold large capitalised stocks, brokers said.
The SET index dropped 11.52 points to 672.48, or down 1.68 percent, on 2.5 billion baht turnover.
The previous lowest close for this year was on March 6 when the index finished at 676.65.
"Investors sold today on concerns that first quarter earnings results of listed firms due to come out next month would be poor," said a broker at a foreign brokerage.
The SET-50 index eased 1.29 points to 50.07.
Decliners overwhelmed gainers 204 to 77 while 100 issues remain unchanged.

Brokers said local mutual funds sold large capitalised banking, energy and communication stocks to cut portfolios ahead of upcoming market holidays. The market will be closed on Thursday for Labour Day and on May 5 for Coronation Day.
"Investors are waiting for the first quarter earnings results of listed firms," said Somnuk Chanrasamee of Nava Finance. Bank and finance firm results were issued last week.
Brokers said the SET index was expected to decline further due to investor worries about the country's high interest rates, despite small cuts on Monday by three banks.
They said cuts on lending rates by 25 basis points, effective on Tuesay, were still not enough.
Large capitalised Bangkok Bank topped the active list, falling four baht to 178. TelecomAsia declined 1.75 to 39.25 and PTT Exploration and Production dropped 14 to 308.
